chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Ali (peace be upon him), when a mawla (client/slave) of his died and left behind relatives, he would not take anything from his inheritance.'
And he would say: 'Those of kinship are closer to one another [in inheritance].'

key_terms.أُولُوا الْأَرْحامِ: Those of kinship (referring to the Quranic verse 33:6)
key_terms.مَوْلًى: Mawla (client or freed slave, dependent on a master or tribe)

ai.seo_question: What is the Imam's share in the inheritance of his mawali if they have living relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s adherence to the Quranic principle of *Ulu al-Arham* (relatives by kinship) over the *Mawali* relationship, demonstrating that the Imam voluntarily forgoes his legal claim to ensure inheritance goes to the deceased's biological family. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s authority is exercised with generosity and strict alignment with divine text, prioritizing blood ties in inheritance distribution.
